key_insight: CAHR reconstructs discrete detector error hypergraphs from syndrome data using exact correlation equations and concurrent pruning, avoiding the false positives common in greedy inference.
engineering_relevance: It offers a practical two-stage workflow for quantum hardware characterization: first recover fault topology, then optimize error probabilities for more reliable decoding.
method: Invert syndrome statistics with exact algebraic correlation equations.
Use a top-down concurrent-pruning strategy to eliminate unphysical error mechanisms.
Separate topology recovery from continuous probability fitting in dense correlated codes.
evidence_signal: In benchmark tests on d=5 rotated surface codes and dense 8-body 2D color codes, CAHR recovered the fault topology without false positives.
watch_item: Exact continuous parameter extraction can still be limited by variance cascade in dense codes, so probability estimates may degrade even when topology is correct.
paper_title: Reconstruction of detector error model for quantum error correction
